newsitem.title: UK: Demand for British Land bond not "as hoped" - SBCW.
newsitem.headline: Demand for British Land bond not "as hoped" - SBCW.

text.p: Demand for British Land Co Plc's 300 million stg 10-year convertible bond was not as hoped, sole lead manager SBC Warburg said in a statement on Wednesday.
"Despite the report on Reuters earlier today, demand for the convertible did not develop as hoped in deteriorating market conditions," the SBC Warburg statement said.
British Land's chairman John Ritblat told Reuters on Tuesday that the deal had met exceptional demand from its target audience of European investors.
At the time, the deal, priced at par with 2.50 points fees, was quoted at 99.875/100.125 on broker screens.
At 0800 GMT it was quoted at 100.75/101.00 while British Land's share price was up 16.5 pence stg, or 2.94 percent, at 577p. The FTSE-100 index was up 14.9 points (0.32 percent) at 4,622.4.
Leading property sector stocks were buoyant after Land Securities announced full year pre-tax profits at the top end of market expectations.

The coupon on the convertible bond was set at 6.50 percent, the top of the indicated 6.25-6.50 percent range. The conversion price was set at 680p per share, a premium of 21.2 percent at the time of pricing to the 561p mid-market share price.
